name: sheetstream
tagline: Read and write million-row XLSX and CSV files in Node.js in about 80 MB of memory
summary: sheetstream reads and writes XLSX and CSV from Node.js without holding the rows in JavaScript. A Rust core does the parsing and zipping and rows cross in batches, so a million-row export fits in a small serverless function. It takes any iterable or async iterable as a source, so a database cursor or a generator works as is.

metrics.source: README.md: The honest summary: memory is a very large win, reading is about 4 times faster than exceljs streaming, and writing is about 2 times faster than the best JS option.

metrics.label: faster writing 1M rows: 5.5 s instead of 12.3 s
metrics.source: README.md: The honest summary: memory is a very large win, reading is about 4 times faster than exceljs streaming, and writing is about 2 times faster than the best JS option.

features: writeXlsx takes any Iterable or AsyncIterable of arrays or objects, and readXlsx is an async iterator of batches
Streaming CSV read and write, plus csvStream, a Node Readable with real backpressure for HTTP responses
XLSX formatting: header style, column widths, per-column number formats, frozen header row and header filter, at no extra memory
Multiple sheets, choose by name or index, with xlsxStream and toBuffer for HTTP and small outputs
Prebuilt binaries for macOS (arm64, x64), Linux (x64 glibc, x64 musl, arm64 glibc) and Windows (x64), nothing to compile on install
how_it_works: Native Rust code (through napi-rs) does the XML, zip and CSV work, so the rows never become JavaScript objects in bulk.
Rows go in and out in batches of 1000 by default, and a parser thread runs a few batches ahead of your loop.
Writing in constant mode streams the sheet XML to a temp file and compresses it into the output, so the cost is disk, not RAM.

notes: Hero: assets/memory.png (3200x1800, dark theme, sheetstream bar in copper). Chart names competitors (exceljs, SheetJS) inside it; if the site must not show competitor names, use the terminal demo clip instead (it also names exceljs). The 'honest summary' sentence quoted for metrics 2 and 3 is the README's own wording. Numbers are from bench/RESULTS.md (Apple M5 Max, Node 24.20, single runs, 1M rows x 10 columns, run 2026-10-05 against sheetstream 0.1.0); not re-run here. Derived ratios: write 12.3/5.5 = 2.2x, read 9.1/2.4 = 3.8x, memory 749/82 = 9.1x vs exceljs streaming and 3270/82 = 40x vs SheetJS (computed from the README tables, not stated there; the stated claims are used as metrics). The demo clip numbers (5.3 s, 79 MB) come from the recorded clip and README demo caption ('exceljs runs out of heap at 1 GB while sheetstream writes 1M rows in 79 MB'). Version 0.3.0 verified via npm view, git tag and GitHub release. Language field: the core is Rust (napi-rs) with a JavaScript API; GitHub reports the repo language as JavaScript. Not verified: Bun support (README says untested); Linux arm64 musl not built. Local checkout dir is xlsx-native; launch kit is in personal/sheetstream-launch (has chart.png identical to assets/memory.png, demo.gif, demo.mp4, demo-x.mp4).
